title: Food Chains
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Food Chains Worksheets (Producers, Predators and Prey)
standard_text: Construct and interpret a variety of food chains, identifying producers, predators and prey.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on food chains: producers, consumers, predators and prey, what the arrows mean, building chains and what happens when numbers change. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Every chain starts with a producer; the arrow points to the eater.
body_html:
How to think about it

A food chain shows what eats what, starting with a producer.

  • Producers (green plants) make food using sunlight. Consumers eat other living things.
  • Arrows point from the food to the animal that eats it: grass → rabbit → fox.
  • Predators hunt prey. If one living thing changes in number, others in the chain are affected.
Example

grass → rabbit → fox. Producer?

The chain starts with it

Answer: grass

Example

If foxes are removed?

Fewer rabbits are eaten

Answer: more rabbits

Common mistakes

  • Drawing arrows pointing to the food instead of the eater.
  • Thinking the producer is an animal.
  • Thinking removing one animal has no effect.

faq.a: A diagram showing what eats what. It starts with a producer, such as a plant, and arrows point to the animals that eat it.
Each arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it, showing the direction energy moves.

faq.q: What happens if one animal is removed?
faq.a: Its prey may increase because fewer are eaten, and its predators may decrease because they have less food.

items.q: Where does the energy in almost every food chain come from first?

items.q: Can an animal be both predator and prey?
c: Yes, for example a blue tit eats caterpillars but is eaten by sparrowhawks.
items.e: Middle of the chain.
